domain: Stipulated binary state, binary signal. Good-state prior p; correct classification probability 4/5; act payoff +6 in good state and -4 in bad; decline payoff 0; observation price c; linear expectation; all actions available before expiry. No measured human or market outcome.
starting_judgment: AV50 proves q=1/2 only for p=1/2,c=1. Its generalization to another prior, to a prior interval, or to a larger policy set has not been established. The hypotheses below include extensions I doubt; they are test targets, not invented previously held beliefs.
prior_basis: The p=1/2 proof is genuine prior evidence. No base rate for these new algebraic claims is available. The confidence numbers are current subjective assessments of the proposed formulas, not calibrated frequencies.
test_rule: Reject a universal claim on one admissible exact countercase. Validate a stated continuum claim only with a complete derivation, checked separately by exact rational state tables and the numeric linear program. A finite passing grid alone leaves the continuum claim unresolved. Preserve all adverse cases.
statistical_scope: These are deterministic identity, optimization and counterexample tests, not a random population sample. Alpha, power, p-values and sample-effect estimates are inapplicable. Conditional on the stipulated premises and a valid exact entailment, a decisive countercase has likelihood zero under that universal; a complete proof settles the stated mathematical domain. No unsupported numerical empirical Bayes factor is assigned.

hypotheses.claim: At c=1, q=1/2 minimizes worst expected regret for every known p in [1/5,4/5], among mixtures of immediate act/decline and all four binary signal response maps.
hypotheses.null: At least one admitted p has another policy with strictly lower worst regret.
hypotheses.prediction: At least the p=1/4 and p=3/5 tests refute H1; the exact optimum need not vary monotonically with p.

hypotheses.claim: For each p in (0,1), every and only binary joint distribution with accuracy 4/5 is (good+ t, good- p-t, bad+ 1/5-p+t, bad- 4/5-t) with max(0,p-1/5)<=t<=min(p,4/5).
hypotheses.null: An admitted joint distribution lies outside the segment, or a point inside it is invalid.
hypotheses.prediction: Each lower endpoint, midpoint and upper endpoint is valid; one rational step outside either endpoint has a negative cell.

hypotheses.claim: For every admitted p in [1/5,4/5] and every matrix of accuracy 4/5, the response act on positive and decline on negative maximizes gross payoff after purchasing the signal.
hypotheses.null: Some admitted matrix has a different fixed signal response map with strictly larger gross payoff.
hypotheses.prediction: High-prior lower endpoints refute H3 because acting after either signal is better there.

hypotheses.claim: For a fixed known p and a fixed mixture of the six admitted pure policies, worst regret over the entire accuracy-4/5 segment is attained at an endpoint.
hypotheses.null: An interior matrix has strictly greater regret than both endpoints.
hypotheses.prediction: Across four unequal policy mixtures per p and 101 t values per mixture, no interior regret exceeds the endpoint maximum; the max-of-affine proof, not this grid, supplies the continuum result.

hypotheses.claim: For known p in [1/5,4/5],c=1, let B=max(0,10p-4), l=2max(0,p-1/5)+4p-9/5, u=2min(p,4/5)+4p-9/5. A minimax policy buys with q=0 when u<=B, q=1 when l>=B and u>B, and q=(u-B)/(u-l) otherwise; its other action attains B and its bought response is act-positive/decline-negative.
hypotheses.null: An admitted six-policy mixture has strictly lower worst regret, or the formula fails at a dominance boundary.
hypotheses.prediction: A six-policy endpoint LP agrees with the exact formula on all four tests, including unequal mixing and a pure-action boundary.

hypotheses.claim: For every known p in [1/5,4/5], accuracy 4/5 and price c>=0, deleting buy-and-act-both, buy-and-decline-both, buy-and-act-negative, and the inferior immediate action leaves a policy set with the same attainable minimax-regret optimum.
hypotheses.null: One deleted action strictly improves minimax regret in an admitted case.
hypotheses.prediction: No deletion raises the LP optimum; zero price permits ties rather than strict dominance for the both/neither maps.

hypotheses.claim: If only p in [2/5,3/5] is known, c=1 and accuracy remains 4/5, the fixed policy half immediate-act and half buy-act-positive has minimax expected regret 3/10 over all admitted (p,t), among mixtures of the six pure policies.
hypotheses.null: That policy exceeds regret 3/10 or another fixed policy has lower worst regret.
hypotheses.prediction: The four corner regrets are 1/10,3/10,3/10,1/10; an independent full-policy LP obtains value3/10.

competing_explanations.account: The half mixture follows from balanced endpoint losses at p=1/2, so a changed prior destroys that balance.
competing_explanations.discriminator: H1,H5; unequal q at noncentral priors.

competing_explanations.account: Any apparent prior effect is an invalid matrix produced by holding sensitivity fixed without maintaining overall accuracy.
competing_explanations.discriminator: H2 exact cell feasibility before every payoff calculation.

competing_explanations.account: An apparent minimax improvement comes from letting signal response depend on the unknown matrix.
competing_explanations.discriminator: H3,H6 and the LP over fixed response maps selected before observing the hidden state or matrix.

competing_explanations.account: An apparent improvement is a numerical or coarse-grid artifact.
competing_explanations.discriminator: Exact rational state sums, endpoint convexity proof, independent floating-point LP.

competing_explanations.account: The policy stays half-and-half but its guarantee worsens when the prior becomes an interval.
competing_explanations.discriminator: H7's unequal regrets across joint-parameter corners and optimum3/10.

competing_explanations.account: The result is caused by implicit human utility preferences or real signal performance.
competing_explanations.discriminator: No such observations enter any test; this account cannot explain the stipulated arithmetic as an observed human effect.

falsification_attempts: Shift p below the act-now threshold.
Move p above the old symmetric point.
Offer all fixed signal response maps to the optimizer.
Search interior likelihoods against endpoint maxima.
Permit a prior interval rather than a known p.
Set zero and larger information prices.
replication_plan: Compare exact state tables, symbolic identities, rational endpoint minimax, an independently constructed six-action LP, and full joint-parameter vertex constraints. Use a later price/prior query after reading the outcomes. Reopen whenever the payoff, signal alphabet, criterion, timing or admissible randomization changes.
